title: Creating a REST Controller
description: Write your first controller and handle HTTP requests.

slides.title: What is a Controller? 🎮
slides.content:
# The Request Handler

A **controller** is a Java class that listens for incoming HTTP requests and returns a response.

In Spring Boot we use annotations to mark controllers and their methods.

slides.title: Your First Controller
slides.content: Create a new class called `HelloController` in the same package as `DemoApplication`. Add the following code:

quizData.question: What does the `@GetMapping("/hello")` annotation do?

options.text: It maps an HTTP POST request to the method
It maps an HTTP GET request to the method at the path `/hello`
It creates a database table named hello

quizData.explanation: `@GetMapping` is a shortcut for `@RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.GET)`. It tells Spring to call this method whenever a GET request is made to `/hello`.

slides.title: Annotation Power 🏷️
slides.content:
## `@RestController` vs `@Controller`

`@RestController` combines `@Controller` and `@ResponseBody`. It means every method returns data directly (like JSON or plain text) instead of a view name. Perfect for REST APIs!
